title: Predicting a projectile's position with constant acceleration
central_question: Where will a moving object be after four seconds if its acceleration stays constant?
learning_outcome: Calculate position and velocity from vector initial conditions and verify displacement independently.
assumptions: Motion is represented in two Cartesian dimensions.
Acceleration is constant throughout the four-second interval.
Position, velocity, and acceleration are expressed in SI units.
solution_narration: The horizontal velocity stays fixed. Vertically, constant downward acceleration changes the velocity from twelve to four metres per second. The average-velocity displacement check independently gives the same final position.
